newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec welcomes lower August unemployment numbers.
newsitem.headline: Quebec welcomes lower August unemployment numbers.

text.p: Quebec's Finance Minister Bernard Landry welcomed Friday's figures from Statistics Canada showing that 41,000 jobs were created during August in the economically depressed province.
"The creation of 41,000 jobs goes in the direction of the majority of economic indicators we have had. But I am still preoccupied by the unemployment rate," Landry said in a statement.
Quebec's unemployment rate fell to 11.8 percent in August, from 12.4 percent in June and July.

Statistics Canada previously reported that Quebec lost a total of 76,000 jobs in just two months -- June and July. The latest figures now show Quebec's job creation level is still 17,000 jobs below the level in January.

"The economy shows indeed some less positive signs -- new home constructions and investments from the public sector," Landry acknowledged. "But encouraging signs are numerous: foreign investments, deliveries, investments from the manufacturing sector, retail sales and confidence of the households," he added
